content: 1. Ustekinumab increases immunosuppressive effects, while maitake decreases them. This interaction may increase the risk of infection. The exact effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Mechlorethamine and ustekinumab may each increase the toxicity of the other due to their immunosuppressive effects, leading to a heightened risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Patients receiving concurrent immunosuppressants or those with compromised immune systems are at an increased risk of serious infections. Caution should be exercised in these cases. 4. Mercaptopurine and ustekinumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Methotrexate and ustekinumab both amplify immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. The formation of CYP450 enzymes can be altered by elevated cytokine levels during chronic inflammation, which may normalize enzyme formation. When initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients on concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, therapeutic effect monitoring should be considered. 7. Ustekinumab and midazolam require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 8. Ustekinumab and minoxidil require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 9. Ofatumumab SC and ustekinumab may increase each other's effects through immunosuppressive mechanisms, raising the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are advised. When switching therapies with immune effects, consider the duration and mechanism of action of these therapies. 10. Ustekinumab and olaparib may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with other myelosuppressive anticancer agents, including DNA-damaging agents, may potentiate and prolong myelosuppressive toxicity. 11. Oxaliplatin and ustekinumab both increase immunosuppressive effects, heightening the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are advised. Using oxaliplatin with concurrent immunosuppressants or in patients with impaired immune systems may increase the risk of serious infections. 12. Ustekinumab and phenobarbital require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 13. Ustekinumab and phenytoin require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 14. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the pneumococcal vaccine (13-valent) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Inactivated vaccinations administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the pneumococcal vaccine (polyvalent) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Inactivated vaccinations administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the inactivated poliovirus vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Vaccination during chemotherapy or radiation therapy should be avoided if possible, as the antibody response may be suboptimal. Patients vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated three months after therapy discontinuation if immune competence has been restored. 17. Ustekinumab and prazosin require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 18. Ustekinumab and primidone require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 19. Ustekinumab and procainamide require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 20. Ustekinumab and quinidine require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 21. Ustekinumab and quinine require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 22. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the rabies vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Inactivated vaccinations administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the rabies vaccine (chick embryo cell-derived) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Inactivated vaccinations administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Rozanolixizumab may decrease the level or effect of ustekinumab through receptor-binding competition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of rozanolixizumab with medications that bind to the human neonatal Fc receptor may lower systemic exposures and effectiveness of such medications. Monitor closely for reduced effectiveness, and consider discontinuing rozanolixizumab if long-term use of such medications is essential. 25. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of sipuleucel-T through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 26. Ustekinumab and sirolimus require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 27. Ustekinumab and tacrolimus require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 28. Ustekinumab and temsirolimus require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 29. Ustekinumab and theophylline require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 30. Ustekinumab and thioridazine require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 31. Ustekinumab and topotecan require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 32. Trastuzumab and ustekinumab may each increase the toxicity of the other through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are recommended. The incidence of neutropenia or febrile neutropenia increased when trastuzumab was co-administered with myelosuppressive chemotherapy. 33. Trastuzumab deruxtecan and ustekinumab may each increase the toxicity of the other through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are recommended. The incidence of neutropenia or febrile neutropenia increased when trastuzumab was co-administered with myelosuppressive chemotherapy. 34. Ublituximab and ustekinumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider the duration of effect and mechanism of action of these therapies if co-administered. 35. Ustekinumab and valproic acid require caution and monitoring due to potential interactions involving CYP450 enzyme modulation. 36. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the zoster vaccine (recombinant) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Immunosuppressive therapies may reduce the effectiveness of the zoster vaccine. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Adalimumab and ustekinumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the adenovirus types 4 and 7 live oral vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations as recommended by current guidelines before initiating therapy. 39. Anakinra and ustekinumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
